name: idsgrep
desc: Grep for Extended Ideographic Description Sequences
why: Greps Ideographic Description Sequences, a door into how CJK characters are composed from components.

brief.what_it_is: IDSgrep is a command-line tool for structural searches over Han-script (CJK) characters. It searches databases of character structure written in an extended form of Unicode Ideographic Description Sequences (IDS), which describe how a character is composed from components. Its example query: find all characters with 月 on the right, which returns 明, 朝, and 期. It uses a query language inspired by traditional Unix regular expressions. The package includes, or can generate, dictionary data from Tsukurimashou, KanjiVG, CHISE, and EDICT2.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a structural kanji search tool from the Tsukurimashou Project, letting users search characters by their component layout rather than by reading or meaning.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage describes IDSgrep as a general tree-matching utility. Character structures are stored as trees in extended IDS notation, and the query language matches patterns against those trees. The homepage does not go into further detail; the user's manual (PDF) is linked from the page but I did not fetch it.
brief.install_notes: The homepage offers a source tarball, idsgrep-0.6.tar.gz (2.9M, dated 2021-03-30), and links to a CI build and Downloads page. I did not read build or dependency instructions. The brew description is the only install-related detail I saw, and no brew-specific caveats were given.
brief.standout: The query language is modelled on Unix regular expressions but applied to character trees rather than strings, so a search can specify where a component sits in a character's layout. It also bundles or generates dictionary data from several character projects.
brief.status: Quiet, with evidence. The latest release on the page is 0.6, dated 2021-03-30. The page itself was updated 2024-01-31 JST, but that date refers to the website, not the software, so it does not show recent development. I did not check a repository commit history.
brief.caveats: I only read the homepage. The README-equivalent manual is a PDF I did not fetch, so command syntax and query details are not confirmed. The homepage has no install commands, and the one release is from 2021. The page is partly in Japanese (a 日本語のページ link exists), though the English page I read is in English.
quotes: IDSgrep is a general tree-matching utility whose main application is to querying databases of Han-script character structures.
For instance, a user might ask for all characters with 月 on the right, and get a result including the characters 明, 朝, and 期.
IDSgrep supports a powerful language for specifying structural queries, inspired by traditional Unix regular expression syntax
fetch_log: https://tsukurimashou.org/idsgrep.php.en: fetched OK; homepage text read. Not a GitHub repo, so no README. The user's manual PDF is linked but I did not follow it (no URL was given in the page text I received). KanjiVG, CHISE and EDICT links are from the page's Links section, which gave labels only; those URLs are my guesses at the sites' home pages and were not fetched.
